title: Fugaro credentials service bundle
description: The document in the credentials service's ONE Secret Manager container (Q6, ruled 2026-10-19): a YAML map of credential names to values, read by the service alone (docs/credentials-service/implementation-plan.md, Task C1.11). The keys are exactly the credentials the platform defines — the model credentials, the GitHub App's private key the mint signs with (C2.1), the upstream Bitbucket credential the git proxy forwards with (D506) and the family of named Bitbucket tokens beside it (D2350), the Bitbucket read consumer the read mint exchanges for a short-lived token (F21), the project's provider key a call to a third-party provider is forwarded with, which carries the two routing facts that call needs and no secret beyond its own (AK6b, D1418), the per-account review-signing keys the verdict routes compute a MAC with (D1069) and one repository's own named credentials — a provider's key held for that repository, or that repository's own Anthropic key (R2, D3008), each carrying the same two routing facts and the marker of the copy that wrote it (D3014) — and the loader refuses a key outside them rather than ignoring it. Written by `fugaro creds set NAME` (C1.25) and by nothing else: no workflow may declare the container's name and `fugaro secrets set` refuses it. A value is never logged, echoed in an error or sent anywhere but to the provider the credential belongs to.
$comment: The bounds mirror internal/credsvc/bundle.go's constants, which are the loader's own rules: maxProperties is MaxBundleCredentials (the wire contract's maxTriedEntries, C1.10), maxLength is MaxBundleValueBytes, and the key pattern is internal/config's credentials as internal/credsvc's CredentialKey reads them (config.GitHubAppKeySecret, config.BitbucketSecret, BitbucketReadConsumerSecret, config.ProviderKeySecret, config.AnthropicSecret, config.ClaudeOAuthToken, config.ClaudeAccountSecret of a name matching config.ClaudeAccountNameRE and config.MaxClaudeAccountNameLen, the review-signing family config.ReviewSigningKeySecret builds and config.ReviewSigningKeyAccount reads back, with the rotation window's -previous entry, and the Bitbucket token family config.BitbucketTokenKey builds and config.BitbucketTokenAccount reads back, D2350, and a service-served key credential's own entry config.CredentialSecret builds and config.CredentialBySecret reads back, D1670/MC23 — the entry is the credential's derived secret name "credential-<name>-key", so its bound is "credential-" (11 bytes) plus MaxClaudeAccountNameLen (31) plus "-key" (4), and a name outside the account rule is one the loader refuses). propertyNames' anyOf gives each family its own whole-name bound, because one number cannot serve all of them: a named account's key is "claude-oauth-token-" (19 bytes) plus at most MaxClaudeAccountNameLen (31), so 50; the review-signing family's current entry adds the review-signing suffix (16 bytes), so 66; the rotation window's previous entry adds -previous (9 bytes) again, so 75; and a named Bitbucket token's key is "bitbucket-token--" (17 bytes, the doubled dash that keeps the family out of the account namespace, R13) plus at most MaxClaudeAccountNameLen, so 48; and a named provider entry's key is "repo-credential--" (17 bytes) plus a repository's slug (63, task.Slug's own bound: a readable part of at most 46 and a 16-hex hash with one dash between them) plus the family's separator (2) plus the longest credential's name the rule admits (config.AnthropicKeyAccount, 26), so 108. The regex alone would admit a dash-heavy account suffix of up to 61 bytes, since each of its {0,30} repetitions may consume two characters, and MaxClaudeAccountNameLen is a check of its own rather than something the pattern carries — so a single bound of 75 for every family would accept a 60-byte account key and a 68-byte review-signing key that the loader refuses. Each branch matches one family and bounds it at that family's longest legal name, so no branch admits a name the loader refuses and none refuses a name it reads. The review-signing family's doubled dash is what keeps it out of the account name space: the account alternation cannot spell one (ClaudeAccountNameRE refuses a doubled dash), so the two cannot be confused and no account name is reserved for it. The Bitbucket token family's doubled dash does the same job for a different collision: claude-oauth-token-bitbucket-token-ci is a legal account today (R13), and a single-dash family would spell that name too, so the doubled dash is what lets the loader read both keys of a document holding them without one name meaning two credentials. A single bound for that family would have the same fault as the account family's: the account regex admits a 61-byte dash-heavy suffix, so the family's own bound of 48 is what refuses what the loader refuses. The `not` beside it is the account family's one reserved spelling, claude-oauth-token-bitbucket-token: it resolves to config.BitbucketSecret, which is already the upstream git credential's key, and CredentialKey refuses it so that one name never means two credentials. `properties` names the two credentials whose value is not a string — the read consumer, a mapping of exactly key, secret and workspace as readConsumerValue reads it, and the provider key, a mapping of exactly key, base_url and auth as providerValue reads it — and naming them there is what exempts them from `additionalProperties`, which still holds every other key of the document to the string shape. `patternProperties` carries a third value that is not a string, and it is the one that cannot be named in `properties`: a named provider entry's key holds the repository it is held for (R2, D3008), so there is one key per repository and credential rather than one spelling, and the pattern is what both selects that shape and holds it to the rule the loader's own reader derives (RepoCredentialKey, RepoCredentialByKey) — "repo-credential--", a repository's slug in task.ValidSlug's shape and without a doubled dash, the family's separator, and a credential that is a provider's name (a letter followed by at most 19 of letter, digit or dash, the local config's own providerNameRE) or config.AnthropicKeyAccount. The entry's value is the provider key's three fields (key, base_url and auth, held to the same rules) plus the optional `source`: the container and version the copy read the value out of (D3014), which is a fact of an entry a copy WROTE, so half a marker and a marker on the project's own key are both refused. This family's `maxLength` is the bound the pattern does not carry, and it is the one family whose pattern states no repetition count of its own: the credential half's length varies (a provider's name is 1 to 20 bytes and the project key's spelling is 26), so no whole-name number can bound the slug half, and JSON Schema cannot put a length on a group in the middle of a pattern. The loader applies the same number to the same whole name (MaxRepoCredentialBytes), so a key it reads and a key this schema admits are still the same set — and a slug longer than a repository's own bound is a name no writer of this family can build, because RepoCredentialKey takes the slug from a verified run's identity. The provider key's `auth` carries the closed set of the two shapes the platform defines (bearer, x-api-key), so the schema is not the weaker reader of a closed set it can state; its `base_url` is deliberately unchecked here, because the rule for one is a config check the loader runs (config.CheckProviderBaseURL: https, or http on a loopback host, no credentials, query, fragment or dot segment) and JSON Schema cannot state it — a pattern would either admit what the loader refuses or, pinning the scheme, refuse the loopback base the loader admits for a local test. This schema is deliberately the weaker of the document's two readers, and the three shapes it accepts that the loader refuses are safe: a YAML alias as a value (`secret: *a`), a scalar carrying a tag other than the string tag (`!!binary`) and a provider base URL the config check refuses. JSON Schema has no notion of the first two — a YAML reader resolves the alias to the node it anchors (which is elsewhere in the document, so a schema that forbade the alias would have to forbid the anchor's own entry) and reads a tagged scalar as the text it spells — while the loader's value branch, readConsumerValue and providerValue require a `!!str` scalar and refuse a node that is not one, so neither shape can reach a credential; the third is not a credential at all, and a bundle the loader refuses never reaches a provider. TestBundleSchemaMatchesTheLoader in internal/credsvc holds the two together, so neither the schema nor the loader can be widened alone.
